title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. He models the generators and relations of SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z) by group schemes over Z. The guiding fact is SL(2,Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, generated by sigma (order 4) and rho (order 6). The stabilizers of the elliptic points i and e^{2pi i/3} are realised as Z-points of the norm-one tori T_sigma (units of Z[i]) and T_rho (units of Z[rho]).

The group schemes involved:
- T_0 = G_m.
- N'_sigma = {1, tau_inf} . T_sigma, the normaliser of the non-split torus T_sigma in GL_2.
- G*_{rho,sigma} sits inside T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma (B'_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma on the previous page).
- M_{rho,sigma}[0] receives the 'trivial' part of the S_3 = <tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf> symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,inf}.

On the previous pages he computed the images of the generators r_0, r_1, r_inf. This page completes the calculation for r_inf = tau_inf' = tau_inf sigma_inf. Its image (39) is (u,a,b) = (-1, 1, tau_inf) in (T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma)(Z), the same element as for r_1 = -tau'_0 up to the sign in T_0.

He then computes integer points (40):
- T_0(Z) = {±1}.
- T_rho(Z) = (Z+Z rho)^* = mu_6 = Z/6, generated by rho.
- T_sigma(Z) = (Z+Z sigma)^* = mu_4 = Z/4, generated by sigma.
- N'_sigma(Z) = {1, tau_inf} ⋉ Z/4 = D_4, the dihedral group of the square, of order 8.

Hence (41): (T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma)(Z) = Z/2 x Z/6 x D_4, of order 96. Here tau_inf acts trivially on the first two factors and by inversion on Z/4.

Next he takes SG*_{rho,sigma}(0)(Z) = {(u,a,b) : det u = det b}. Since det b = ±1 = T_0(Z), u is determined by b. So this group is isomorphic to (T_rho x N'_sigma)(Z) = Z/6 x D_4, of order 48.

Marginal note (42): the further condition det a = eps' det u with eps'^2 = 1 is automatic over Z, because G_m(Z) = {±1}.

A struck line begins a map D_4 -> M_{rho,sigma}[0](Z), with {tau_inf^i sigma^j}. The next page uses all this to write M_{rho,sigma}(Z) as a semidirect product of a finite group with SL(2,Z), and to compute the determinant-type map to mu_2 x mu_2 on integer points.

Purpose: to identify concretely the integral points of his group-scheme model of the symmetry group of the 'loop equation' / the (2,3,inf) triangle structure, and to check that the S_3 symmetries tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf land in the expected finite subgroup.
errors: 'D_4 groupe diédral d'ordre 4' means the dihedral group of the square (degree 4), which has order 8. This is a naming convention, not an error, but it could mislead.
The semidirect-product notation in (41), (Z/2).(Z/2 x Z/6 x Z/4), with tau_inf acting by symmetry only on Z/4, is consistent. The order-96 count is correct.
The identification SG*(0)(Z) = Z/6 x D_4 is correct given det: T_0 -> G_m being the identity and det b ∈ {±1}.
Possible convention inconsistency across pages: tau_inf is written as (0 1;1 0) on p.504 and as diag(-1,1) on p.407. This affects only presentation, not this page's calculation.

ideas.what: Unit groups of the Gaussian and Eisenstein integers as Z-points of non-split tori, Z/4 and Z/6, realising the elliptic stabilisers of SL(2,Z)
ideas.modern_name: Integral points of norm-one tori / finite subgroups of SL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gauss, Klein; Serre 'Trees' for the amalgam)

ideas.what: Normaliser of the non-split torus T_sigma in GL_2 having integer points D_4 = {1, tau_inf} ⋉ Z/4
ideas.modern_name: Normaliser of a non-split Cartan subgroup, integral points

ideas.what: Group-scheme-over-Z model (G*_{rho,sigma}, M_{rho,sigma}) of the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 and of the S_3 symmetries of P^1 - {0,1,inf}, with explicit computation of its integral points
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic / integral-group-scheme model of SL2(Z), GL2(Z) as an amalgam of tori normalisers; related to Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type symmetry analysis
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (no standard modern counterpart known to me)

missed.claim: An explicit device in Grothendieck's unpublished 'équation des lacets' work: SL(2,Z)/GL(2,Z) and their finite stabilisers are encoded through Z-group schemes built from the tori of Z[i] and Z[rho] and the normaliser of the Gaussian torus. Integral points are computed (orders 96 and 48), and the images of tau_0, tau_1, tau_inf are located inside them. The idea of an integral group-scheme envelope of the (2,3,inf) amalgam does not seem to have a standard counterpart in the literature, but the computations on this page themselves are routine.
missed.quote: SG^*_{ρ,σ}(0)(Z) = {(u,a,b) | det u = det b} ≃ (T_ρ × N'_σ)(Z) ≃ Z/6Z × D_4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild historical interest for reconstructing how Grothendieck intended to treat the loop equation / GT-type relations scheme-theoretically over Z. Not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an elementary bookkeeping computation of integral points of tori and the dihedral normaliser. The framework it serves (group-scheme models of the amalgam over Z) is somewhat unusual but is not developed here.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'c'est toujours le même élément' (the same element as for r_1), rather than 'la = δième'.
The struck text after SG*_{ρ,σ}(0)(Z) = is 'T_{ρ,σ}' (crossed out); in the next line the crossed-out symbol is 'D_4', leaving '≃ (T_ρ × N'_σ)(Z) ≃ Z/6Z × D_4'.

Marginal note: 'NB la condition det a = ε' det u, ε'^2 = 1 est automatiquement vérifiée, car G_m(Z) = {±1}' (42). The words 'NB la condition' belong to this margin note, not to the main line 'D'autre part'.
Bottom struck lines: 'et flèche principale [?] D_4 → M_{ρ,σ}[0](Z), τ_∞ ; {τ_∞^i σ^j | i ∈ Z/2Z, j ∈ Z/4Z}'.
